facts.fact: The adwave.com guide 'Small Business Backups: The Complete Guide for 2026' was published on June 2, 2026.
The guide states that sync is not the same as backup because sync works like a mirror that can copy deletions, corruption, or ransomware encryption to every copy.
facts.quote: Sync is not the same as backup. Sync works like a mirror. If a file is deleted, corrupted, or encrypted by ransomware, the mirror can copy the problem too.

facts.fact: The guide defines backup as a copy existing and recovery as being able to put that copy back into use fast enough to keep the business running.
facts.quote: Backup means a copy exists. Recovery means you can put that copy back into use fast enough to keep the business running.

facts.fact: The guide's practical rule says that if losing a file would interrupt sales, billing, delivery, or customer service, a backup copy should be kept that can be restored on demand.
facts.quote: If losing a file would interrupt sales, billing, delivery, or customer service, keep a backup copy you can restore on demand.

facts.fact: The guide says a useful backup plan should answer three questions: what to protect first, how much recent work the business can afford to lose, and how quickly access is needed again.
facts.quote: What do we protect first?

facts.fact: According to the guide's summary of Splunk's overview, backup design has moved beyond simple duplication toward adversary-aware recovery, where immutable backups and offline storage are treated as important ransomware defenses.
facts.quote: emphasizes that backup design has moved beyond simple duplication toward

facts.fact: The guide defines a hybrid backup as combining local and cloud backup, so one copy is fast to restore and another survives local trouble.
facts.quote: A **hybrid backup** does both.

facts.fact: The guide notes that local backups are exposed when fire, theft, flood, or ransomware affects the same environment as the original data.
facts.quote: Fire, theft, flood, or ransomware in the same environment can affect both the original and the backup.

facts.fact: The guide states that cloud backup's tradeoffs are that large restores can take longer and recovery depends on the provider setup and internet access.
facts.quote: large restores can take longer, and recovery depends on your provider setup and internet access.

facts.fact: The 3-2-1 backup rule calls for 3 copies of your data.
facts.quote: 3 copies of your data

facts.fact: The 3-2-1 backup rule calls for 2 different types or locations of storage.
facts.quote: 2 different types or locations of storage

facts.fact: The 3-2-1 backup rule calls for 1 copy kept off-site.
facts.quote: 1 copy kept off-site

facts.fact: Some businesses extend the 3-2-1 rule to 3-2-1-1, which adds one copy that is isolated or locked against change, according to the page's description.
facts.quote: with one copy that is isolated or locked against change

facts.fact: A full backup is a complete copy of every folder, which is the easiest to understand and restore but takes more time and storage.
facts.quote: A full backup is a complete photocopy of every folder in the cabinet.

facts.fact: An incremental backup copies only what changed since the last backup of any kind.
facts.quote: An incremental backup copies only what changed since the last backup of any kind.

facts.fact: A differential backup copies what changed since the last full backup.
facts.quote: A differential backup copies what changed since the last full backup.
